findings.title: Backup-code login is rejected for users whose identityProvider is not CAL
findings.body: The guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the new backup-code branch. A Google/SAML user with twoFactorEnabled who submits a backup code (and therefore no totpCode) gets the 'account created with identity provider' error instead of having the backup code verified — the condition was not extended to also allow `credentials.backupCode`. This user class is real: the signIn callback converts CAL accounts to Google/SAML while keeping twoFactorEnabled and backupCodes, and then routes them through the /auth/login?totp= (loginWithTotp) flow. It is compounded by apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx, which renders ExternalTotpFooter (no 'Lost access' button) for that flow, so these users have no way to use their backup codes at all and are permanently locked out if they lose their authenticator.

findings.title: Backup codes are shown exactly once with no recovery path, and the dialog can be dismissed at that step
findings.body: handleEnable() enables 2FA on the server and only then moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step. At that step the dialog can still be closed without using the Close/Copy/Download buttons (dialog close control / Escape / overlay via onOpenChange), and resetState() is only wired to the Cancel and Close buttons, not to onOpenChange — so component state is also left stale (step stays DisplayBackupCodes with the old codes). The codes are never retrievable again: the totp/setup endpoint rejects users who already have twoFactorEnabled, and this PR adds no regeneration UI or API. A user who closes the wizard before saving the codes (and likewise all users who enabled 2FA before this feature and have backupCodes=null) has no way to obtain codes, and is locked out if they later lose their authenticator. Completion should be gated on an explicit confirmation and/or a regenerate-codes endpoint should exist.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message tells users to generate codes in settings, which is impossible
findings.body: The string "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." is shown when a 2FA-enabled user has no stored backup codes — i.e. every user who enabled 2FA before this feature — both in the login flow and in the disable-2FA modal. No settings UI or API exists to generate backup codes after initial setup (the setup endpoint rejects already-enabled users), so the instruction cannot be followed; users who lost their authenticator are directed to a nonexistent capability instead of being told to disable/re-enable 2FA or contact support.

findings.title: Backup-code single-use guarantee is not enforced under concurrent requests
findings.body: Code consumption is a read-modify-write: decrypt the stored array, indexOf the supplied code, set that slot to null, re-encrypt and update the user row — with no transaction, lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same valid backup code can both read the array before either writes, both pass indexOf, and both be authenticated, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' promise made in the UI copy (backup_code_instructions). A transaction or an atomic update would close the window.

findings.title: No test exercises logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA with one
findings.body: The added e2e steps only verify that the backup-codes screen renders, the download filename, and the copy toast. The core behavior of the feature — a successful login with a backup code, rejection of a wrong code, single-use consumption (the code is invalidated after use in next-auth-options.ts), and disabling 2FA with a backup code — has no automated coverage, and the PR checklist explicitly states tests proving the feature works were not added. A regression in the authorize or disable logic would ship unnoticed.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order in the shared PasswordField
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button removes it from the tab order in every place the shared PasswordField is used (login, password change, 2FA setup/disable, etc.). Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the control to verify what they typed, which is an accessibility regression for a security-relevant input. If the intent was to fix tab order into the 2FA digit inputs of one specific form, the change should be scoped to that form rather than the shared component.
